item: PySocks is a core dependency, so Tor works out of the box; the Wikidata getters say separate circuits, not unlinkable lookups (queue items 68(d) and 68(b))
summary: Queue items 68(d) and 68(b), ruled R656 on #1918's follow-ups. 68(d) BEFORE: protected mode over Tor needs PySocks (requests reaches a socks5h:// proxy through urllib3.contrib.socks), but no install carried it: pyproject.toml and requirements.lock left it out, docs/SECURITY.md told the operator to pip install pysocks ("no packaged extra"), and only CI's test job installed it, in a step of its own, so the SOCKS airplane-guard tests ran there and skipped in core-only. Without it every protected-mode fetch over a SOCKS proxy fails at once with requests' InvalidSchema "Missing dependencies for SOCKS support" (it fails closed: no clearnet fallback), and the airplane guard's two PySocks patches (socksocket.connect and sendto) have nothing to wrap. NOW: PySocks>=1.7.1 is a core dependency, pinned in requirements.lock at 1.7.1 with the three sha256 hashes PyPI lists for that release (the py3 wheel, the py27 wheel, the sdist); CI's separate install step is gone, since every lane now installs it with the project, so the socks-gated tests also run in core-only; docs/SECURITY.md and the comments in src/ingest/__init__.py, airplane.py, ssrf_guard.py and fetch_verdict.py, and in tests/test_refusal_wrapped_shape.py, say it is core; the shard mutant in tests/test_skipped_tests_have_a_ci_job_that_runs_them.py takes a [geo]-gated file as its example, because a socks-gated one is now covered in every lane. 68(b): the Wikidata getters' docstrings (src/analytics/ring_loader.py, src/catalog/wikidata_apply.py, and the comment in src/api/source_management.py that leans on them) said distinct lookups were unlinkable over Tor. They now say each lookup asks for a separate circuit (true from #1918, queue item 50(a), which this branch carries: before it every Wikidata URL kept the same first 32 characters and so one SOCKS credential), and that separate circuits do not make the lookups unlinkable: each sends a bot User-Agent (guarded_session sets the caller's User-Agent in protected mode too) and the lookups run close together, so Wikidata can still tie them to one another. TESTS: tests/test_pysocks_dependency_item68.py, 6: PySocks imports at 1.7.1 or later; requests uses urllib3's real SOCKSProxyManager, not its stand-in; an adapter builds a SOCKS manager for a Tor proxy without connecting; the airplane guard holds PySocks to wrap; core declares it and the lock pins it with hashes; no module under src/ says separate circuits make lookups unlinkable. This sandbox has no PySocks, so the first four fail here, which is the case they exist to catch; against a stand-in socks module on the path (a check of the tests' own logic, never shipped) all 6 pass; CI installs the real one. An independent read: GO for 68(d); for 68(b) a must-fix (the separate-circuit sentence was false on a base without #1918; this branch merges #1918 first) and should-fixes (three stale PySocks comments, folded; the protected-mode User-Agent below). NOT CHANGED, stated: guarded_session sends the caller's bot User-Agent in protected mode, while docs/SECURITY.md, docs/USER_MANUAL.md and the Settings note say protected mode sends a generic one (pre-existing, outside R656; sent to the coordinator for a ruling); the airplane guard still tolerates PySocks' absence (an install made without dependencies); R656's (a) leaves per-URL isolation as it is and (c) is note-only. Release-notes line: «Tor works out of the box: PySocks, the library the app needs to reach a SOCKS proxy such as Tor, is now installed with the app instead of by hand.»
